headline: Carry each partial path and its running sum
statement: Return all root-to-leaf paths whose node values sum to targetSum. Each returned path is a list of node values in root-to-leaf order. Return paths in any order. Distinct root-to-leaf routes with identical values contribute separate, repeated entries.
intuition: Carry each partial path and its running sum. A matching sum is an answer only when the path has reached a leaf.
approach: Use an explicit stack containing node, prefix path, and prefix sum.
Append the current value and update the sum.
Emit a path only if both children are absent and the sum matches.
Push children with the updated prefix state.
correctness: The stack state records the unique root-to-parent path for its node. Adding the node creates its unique root-to-node path. Every leaf is visited exactly once and only matching leaf paths are emitted; no partial or non-root path is included.
bruteForce: Copy and sum every root-to-leaf path independently, repeating prefix work.

complexity.explanation: n is node count, h is height, and L is the total number of returned path values. Copying a prefix at each visited node costs O(n*h), with a quadratic chain worst case. At most O(h) pending binary-tree DFS entries retain paths of length O(h), so auxiliary storage is O(h²); returned lists use O(L).

pitfalls: Do not accept a matching internal node.
Negative values mean an oversized prefix cannot be pruned.
Distinct nodes can yield identical value paths and both count.
